method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited texts with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; two seat-neutral cores (voc-core.l4, the Victims of Crime Act Part 4 with four regulative rules: ss 18(1)-(4), 18(5)-(6) with 19(2), 19(2)-(3), 21(1); ctp-core.l4, the Motor Vehicles Act Part 4 notice and nominal defendant rules and the Civil Liability Act Part 8 limits, with three regulative rules: s 126A(1)-(2) with reg 4, s 126A(4), s 126A(5)), a shared arithmetic module (voc-common.l4), and two seat layers that restate no rule (voc-seat.l4 for the injured person, voc-seat-insurer.l4 for the CTP insurer and the nominal defendant); joined by Victims of Crime Act s 17(5)(c); no REFUSE (an offence before 1 July 2015, an accident before 1 July 2013, legal costs for proceedings before 25 July 2019, service for a court application before 2 September 2019, an application's contents before 11 May 2023, a CTP notice's contents before 1 November 2021, a scale value or ISV out of range, an unprescribed limited-claim cost or another State's CTP scheme answers `not covered`, asserted); fixed on 2026-10-24 after an independent verifier's report (NOTES.md findings 20-27); checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: All from the Open Australian Legal Corpus (South Australian legislation last collected 2025-03-10), not the official texts, and possibly out of date: Victims of Crime Act 2001 as at 2021-01-01 (listed at 1.4.2025, so a later version exists), ../../registers/source-bundle/victims-of-crime-act-2001.txt; Victims of Crime (Statutory Compensation) Regulations 2019 as at 2023-05-11; Motor Vehicles Act 1959 as at 2024-11-07; Motor Vehicles (Third Party Insurance) Regulations 2013 as at 2021-11-01; Civil Liability Act 1936 as at 2023-06-22; Civil Liability Regulations 2013 as at 2015-10-02; each deposited at subjects/au/sa/<slug>/registers/source-bundle/<slug>.txt. CPI figures, State average weekly earnings and the court's assessments are inputs.

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run voc-common.l4 ; l4 run voc-core.l4 ; l4 run ctp-core.l4 ; l4 run voc-seat.l4 ; l4 run voc-seat-insurer.l4 ; l4 run voc-cases-injured.l4 ; l4 run voc-cases-insurer.l4
checks.result: 270 assertions satisfied (222 in voc-cases-injured.l4, 48 in voc-cases-insurer.l4, of which 17 mirror assertions), 0 errors, 0 warnings (2026-10-24, after the fix); 8 #TRACEs with an expect line (6 breaches, 5 by the claimant and 1 by the insurer; 2 obligations pending), each read and as expected; negative controls (Schedule a1 row 14 raised by $1; after the fix, reg 7 truncating and the 2019 Regulations' first day moved: 4 of 222 failed as predicted) were caught
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: In: Victims of Crime Act 2001 s 4(1), (2); s 17(1)-(5) (s 17(6) as a note); s 18 (not (4a)); s 19(2), (3); s 20(1), (3), (5), (5a), (7), (9); s 21(1), (2); s 25(1); s 34; Schedule a1; Victims of Crime (Statutory Compensation) Regulations 2019 reg 4, Schedule 1, reg 5, Schedule 2 cll 2, 3, 3A. Motor Vehicles Act 1959 s 99(3), (3a), s 104(1)(a), s 115(1), (3), (4), s 116(1), (2), (4), (5), s 126A; Motor Vehicles (Third Party Insurance) Regulations 2013 regs 4-6. Civil Liability Act 1936 s 3(1) (terms used), s 51, s 52(1), (3)-(8), s 53, s 54, s 56, s 56A(2), (3), (5)-(9), s 58(1)(a), (2)-(4), s 58B(3); Civil Liability Regulations 2013 reg 7 (an ISV rounded to a whole number, a half up), regs 18, 19. Each answer only where the deposited version applies (NOTES.md, Coverage dates). Out: VOCA Parts 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 (except s 34), ss 18(4a), 19(1), 20(2), (6), (10), (11), 21(3)-(5), 22-24, 25(2), 26, Schedule 1, Regulations Sch 2 cl 4 and reg 6; the rest of MV Act Part 4, s 99(4), other States' CTP law; CLA Parts 1-7 and 9, s 52(2) (non-motor negligence), ss 55, 56A(4), 57, 58(1)(b), (5), (6), 58A, 58B(2), 76; CL Regulations Part 2 beyond reg 7, Schedule 1, Parts 4 and 5. Read with subjects/au/social-security-act-1991 (Part 3.14 compensation: unverified), subjects/au/sa/return-to-work-act-2014 (s 17(5)(b), (6)); cross-folder IMPORT is not possible.
seats: the injured person: the victim of an offence, or a family member claiming for grief, the dependants' financial loss or funeral expenses; or a person injured in a motor accident
the CTP insurer (Motor Vehicles Act s 126A(4)-(5), which also bind the nominal defendant)
